summary: Punta Chivato Airport (PCV) is a small regional airstrip serving the remote Punta Chivato peninsula along Mexico's Sea of Cortez in Baja California Sur. It primarily supports general aviation, private pilots, and access to the surrounding coastal developments and eco-tourism areas near Mulegé. The airport's isolation makes it a convenient gateway for travelers seeking the area's uncrowded beaches, tidal pools, and desert-meets-sea landscapes.
faqs:
Q: Is Punta Chivato Airport open to public flights?
A: Yes, it operates as a public-use small airport, though it has no scheduled commercial service.

Q: Are there customs facilities at PCV?
A: No customs or immigration services are available; international arrivals would need to clear at a designated port of entry first.

Q: What is the runway surface like?
A: The airport has a single unpaved or semi-improved runway typical of remote Baja airstrips, suitable primarily for small general aviation aircraft.

Q: Can I rent a car at the airport?
A: No rental car counters operate on-site; visitors typically arrange ground transport in advance through local accommodations.
transport_tips: Ground transportation is not available on demand, so arrange a pickup with your lodging or a local guide before arrival. The drive to Mulegé takes roughly 45 minutes via unpaved desert roads, so a high-clearance vehicle is recommended. Many visitors fly in with their own aircraft and pre-stage ground vehicles, as rental services are essentially nonexistent in the area.
local_tip: Time your visit around low tide—the exposed tidal pools and sandbars around Punta Chivato reveal some of the best shelling and marine viewing on the Sea of Cortez, and they're just a short drive from the airstrip.
